source: Public view counts (data/latest-videos.json, data/past-performance.json) and YouTube Studio's AI analysis of 21 Nov 2026. View counts on the page are read live from those files.
headline: Two pillars work, and YouTube's own AI agrees: (1) practical, cost-saving dev tooling, and (2) grounded long-form career and industry takes with a data angle. What doesn't work is mindset Shorts and narrow commentary.

works.title: Pillar 1 · Practical, cost-saving dev tooling
works.short: Cheap model + one trick = frontier results
works.why: It solves a problem the viewer has today (cost, a weak model, a missing feature) and they can copy it in minutes. YouTube's AI calls this 'pragmatic, cost-conscious dev tooling'.
recipe: Open on the money or the pain: 'Don't pay $200…', '…for $0', 'X missing?'
Name the exact tool and model (Kilo Code, DeepSeek, LSP, Claude)
Show it working on screen within 10 seconds
End by pointing to the long-form parent video or the Skool setup file

examples.title: Stop Paying for Claude: Make Qwen Code Like a Frontier Model in Kilo
examples.hook: This model costs a fraction of Claude, and it just passed my test suite.
beats: 0:05 the one config change in Kilo Code

examples.title: Your Cheap AI Model Is Blind. Give It an MCP Server in 60 Seconds
examples.hook: Your cheap model fails because it can't see your project, not because it's dumb.
beats: 0:45 point to Skool for the config

examples.title: Frontier-Level AI Coding for Under $10 a Month (Full Setup)
examples.format: 📹 Long · 10–12 min · the parent for the Shorts
examples.hook: My AI coding bill last month was [your real number]. Here's the whole setup.
beats: The stack: model, Kilo, LSP, MCP
Call to action: Skool config + Delivery Pilot course

works.title: Pillar 2 · Grounded career & industry takes, with data
works.short: Hype claim → 'the data says otherwise' → what to do
works.why: It cuts through hype with evidence and a realistic engineering view, then tells the viewer what to do. YouTube's AI says these earn your highest overall views and watch time.
recipe: Open with a big claim plus a contrarian, data-backed answer
Cite real sources and say where the evidence stops
Give one framework per video (not five)
End with a concrete plan (e.g. 90 days) and a call to action

examples.title: Junior Dev Jobs Are Down 50%. Here's How to Become a Delivery Pilot in 90 Days

beats: Why it's a dip, not the end
What AI took vs what stays human

examples.hook: I never finished my degree. In 2027 that matters less, and here's the data.
beats: Hiring data on degrees vs skills

alsoWorks.title: Also strong: practical AI builds for a job-seeker outcome
alsoWorks.detail: Your all-time #1 is a build, and the newest one is your fastest grower. These sit where both pillars meet: a practical tool aimed at a career result.

examples.title: Build an AI That Tailors Your CV to Every Job Ad (n8n, Free)
examples.hook: Sending the same CV to every job doesn't work. This agent rewrites yours for each one.

examples.title: I Let AI Coach Me Through a Live System Design Interview
examples.format: 📹 Long · 8 min · follow-up to the Interview Overlay
examples.hook: Your fastest-growing video, part 2: the overlay against a real interview question.
beats: Where it helped, where it didn't

doesnt.title: Mindset Shorts
doesnt.short: A slogan with no tool and no data
doesnt.why: In 45 seconds there's nothing to copy and nothing to prove. Viewers swipe past a slogan. The Delivery Pilot idea does land, but only inside a practical video, as its closing line.
doesnt.instead: Put the mindset line at the end of a tool Short, or make it a long-form take with data (Pillar 2).

rewrites.after: Rider, Driver or Pilot? Watch Me Ship the Same Feature All 3 Ways
rewrites.why: Turns the slogan into a demo: three screen recordings, three timings.

rewrites.after: I Asked 3 AIs to Cut a Security Corner. Here's Who Said No.
rewrites.why: Values shown through a test with stakes, not stated.

rewrites.after: I Never Finished My Degree. This AI Skill Replaced It for Me
rewrites.why: Your real story with stakes, the shape of the one mindset Short that worked (148).

doesnt.title: Narrow or general commentary
doesnt.short: A personal or niche angle with no clear payoff
doesnt.why: The topic is either too niche to be searched ('red tape') or too general to stand out ('AI isn't a bubble', habits). Neither has a hook that makes a developer click.
doesnt.instead: Choose a topic people search for and add data, or turn it into a build.

rewrites.after: Use AI to Decode Any Confusing Form in 2 Minutes (Visa, Tax, HR)
rewrites.why: Searchable and practical, and the visa angle ties back to your immigrant story.

rewrites.after: AI Isn't a Bubble: 5 Numbers That Prove It (2026 Data)
rewrites.why: Same opinion, now with a data angle (Pillar 2).

rewrites.after: My 10-Minute Daily AI Routine to Learn Any Tech (Obsidian Setup)
rewrites.why: Turns a habit story into a tool workflow someone can copy (Pillar 1).

exceptions.note: A mindset Short that did work (148). It's a story with something at stake ('I walked in anyway'), not a slogan.
An explainer that worked (142) next to one on the same topic that didn't ('AI Doesn't Read Words', 23). Clear packaging beat a vague hook.
